# CaratBase

> CaratBase is a free, independent jewelry valuation reference. It shows what a diamond, gemstone or piece of gold jewelry is actually worth — both the retail figure a jeweler would charge and the resale range you would realistically be offered when you sell. No account, no sign-up, $0.

CaratBase does not buy or sell jewelry and is not a licensed appraiser. Figures are estimates for information, not an appraisal or an offer.

## Tools
- [Value my diamond & jewelry](https://caratbase.com/value.html): center stone, side stones and metal priced as a whole piece, with retail and resale.
- [GIA report value](https://caratbase.com/gia-report-value.html): enter the grades from a grading report to get retail and resale, and see which grades cost the most.
- [Gemstone values](https://caratbase.com/gemstone.html): ruby, sapphire, emerald, tanzanite and more; treatment matters more than size.
- [Gold & metal prices](https://caratbase.com/metals.html): live spot per gram for every karat, refreshed automatically.
- [Scrap gold calculator](https://caratbase.com/scrap-gold-calculator.html): melt value in grams, pennyweight or troy ounces and whether an offer is fair.
- [Class ring value](https://caratbase.com/class-ring-value-calculator.html): check the stamp and weight for the real melt figure.
- [Hallmark lookup](https://caratbase.com/stamp.html): what 925, 750, 585, GF, EPNS and other stamps mean.
- [Diamond budget calculator](https://caratbase.com/budget.html): the biggest stone a budget buys, four ways, with resale.
- [Compare two diamonds](https://caratbase.com/compare.html): size, price, resale and price per carat side by side.
- [Lab-grown vs natural](https://caratbase.com/lab-vs-natural.html): cost today and value in five years.
- [Ring size converter](https://caratbase.com/ring-size.html) and [Measure from a photo](https://caratbase.com/measure.html).
- [My vault](https://caratbase.com/vault.html): saved pieces stay on the user's own device.

## Method
- [How we value](https://caratbase.com/methodology.html): per-carat curve with jumps at popular weights, multipliers for color, clarity, cut and shape against a G/VS2/Very Good round baseline, a lab-grown factor and an uncertified discount. Resale currently 25–40% of retail for natural diamonds and 5–12% for lab-grown.
- Limits: a price model cannot see damage, fluorescence, brand or antique value. For insurance, probate or legal use, get a certified appraisal.
